arxiv-1809-07700.title: ReSyst: a novel technique to Reduce the Systematic uncertainty for precision measurements
arxiv-1809-07700.creator: P. Van Mulders
arxiv-1809-07700.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by P. Van Mulders. We are in an era of precision measurements at the Large Hadron Collider. The precision that can be achieved on some of those is limited however due to large systematic uncertainties. This paper introduces a new technique to reduce the total systematic uncertainty by quantifying the systematic impact of single events and correlating it with event observables to identify classes of events that are more sensitive to systematic effects.

arxiv-2110-14892.title: Analysis of COVID-19 in Japan with Extended SEIR model and ensemble Kalman filter
arxiv-2110-14892.creator: Q. Sun🖂, T. Miyoshi, S. Richard
arxiv-2110-14892.description: Abstract We introduce an extended SEIR infectious disease model with data assimilation for the study of the spread of COVID-19. In this framework, undetected asymptomatic and pre-symptomatic cases are taken into account, and the impact of their uncertain proportion is fully investigated.

arxiv-2111-10286.title: HI in and behind the Hubble Frontier Field Clusters: A Deep MeerKAT Pilot Search out to z ∼ 0.5 z\sim 0.5 2015 HI in and behind the Hubble Frontier Field Clusters: A Deep MeerKAT Pilot Search out to z ∼ 0.5 z\sim 0.5 – References

arxiv-2111-10286.description: Abstract The Hubble Frontier Fields (HFF) are a selection of well-studied galaxy clusters used to probe dense environments and distant gravitationally lensed galaxies. We explore the 21cm neutral hydrogen ( H i ) content of galaxies in three of the HFF clusters, Abell 2744 ( z z = 0.308), Abell S1063 ( z z = 0.

arxiv-2207-09783.title: Cancer Subtyping by Improved Transcriptomic Features Using Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder
arxiv-2207-09783.creator: Zheng Chen, Ziwei Yang, Lingwei ZhuGuang Shi, Kun Yue, Takashi Matsubara, Shigehiko Kanaya, MD Altaf-Ul-Amin
arxiv-2207-09783.description: Abstract Defining and separating cancer subtypes is essential for facilitating personalized therapy modality and prognosis of patients. The definition of subtypes has been constantly recalibrated as a result of our deepened understanding. During this recalibration, researchers often rely on clustering of cancer data to provide an intuitive visual reference that could reveal the intrinsic characteristics of subtypes.

arxiv-2210-07107.title: A note on the action with the Schwarzian at the stretched horizon
arxiv-2210-07107.creator: Mohd Ali
arxiv-2210-07107.description: Abstract Abstract In this paper, we discuss the quantization of an interesting model of Carlip which appeared recently. It shows a way to associate boundary degrees of freedom to the stretched horizon of a stationary non-extremal black hole, as has been done in JT gravity for near-extremal black holes.

arxiv-2301-12894.title: F F -transforms determined by overlap and grouping maps over a complete lattice
arxiv-2301-12894.creator: Abha Tripathi, S.P. Tiwari, Sutapa Mahato
arxiv-2301-12894.description: Abstract This paper is about the study of F F -transforms based on overlap and grouping maps, residual and co-residual implicator over complete lattice from both constructive and axiomatic approaches. Further, the duality, basic properties, and the inverse of proposed F F -transforms have been studied, and axiomatic characterizations of proposed direct F F -transforms are investigated.

arxiv-2310-10638.title: In-Context Pretraining: Language Modeling Beyond Document Boundaries
arxiv-2310-10638.creator: Weijia Shi, Sewon Min, Maria Lomeli, Chunting Zhou, Margaret Li, Gergely Szilvasy, Rich James, Xi Victoria Lin, Noah A. Smith, Luke Zettlemoyer, Scott Yih, Mike Lewis
arxiv-2310-10638.description: Abstract Large language models (LMs) are currently trained to predict tokens given document prefixes, enabling them to directly perform long-form generation and prompting-style tasks which can be reduced to document completion. Existing pretraining pipelines train LMs by concatenating random sets of short documents to create input contexts but the prior documents provide no signal for predicting the next document.

arxiv-2405-01624.title: The LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey: The nature of the faint source population and SFR-radio luminosity relation using Prospector
arxiv-2405-01624.creator: Soumyadeep Das, Daniel J. B. Smith, Paul Haskell, Martin J. Hardcastle, Philip N. Best, Kenneth J. Duncan, Marina I. Arnaudova, Shravya Shenoy, Rohit Kondapally, Rachel K. Cochrane, Alyssa B. Drake, Gülay Gürkan, Katarzyna Małek, Leah K. Morabito, Isabella Prandoni
arxiv-2405-01624.description: Abstract Spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting has been extensively used to determine the nature of the faint radio source population. Recent efforts have combined fits from multiple SED-fitting codes to account for the host galaxy and any active nucleus that may be present.

arxiv-2405-18033.title: RT-GS2: Real-Time Generalizable Semantic Segmentation for 3D Gaussian Representations of Radiance Fields
arxiv-2405-18033.creator: Mihnea-Bogdan Jurca*, Remco Royen*, Ion Giosan, Adrian Munteanu
arxiv-2405-18033.description: Abstract Gaussian Splatting has revolutionized the world of novel view synthesis by achieving high rendering performance in real-time. Recently, studies have focused on enriching these 3D representations with semantic information for downstream tasks. In this paper, we introduce RT-GS2, the first generalizable semantic segmentation method employing Gaussian Splatting.

arxiv-2409-06777.title: Black hole–neutron star binaries with high spins and large mass asymmetries: II. Properties of dynamical simulations
arxiv-2409-06777.creator: Konrad Topolski, Samuel D. Tootle, Luciano Rezzolla
arxiv-2409-06777.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Konrad Topolski, Samuel D. Tootle, Luciano Rezzolla. Black hole (BH) – neutron star (NS) binary mergers are not only strong sources of gravitational waves (GWs), but they are also candidates for joint detections in the GW and electromagnetic (EM) spectra. However, the possible emergence of an EM signal from these binaries relies crucially on the fate of the NS which, in turn, is determined by a complex combination of the equation of state (EOS), the BH spin, and the mass ratio.

arxiv-2409-07309.title: A Geodetic and Astrometric VLBI Experiment at 22/43/88/132 GHz Facilities: KVN, EAVN
arxiv-2409-07309.creator: Shuangjing Xu, Taehyun Jung, Bo Zhang, Ming Hui Xu, Do-Young Byun, Xuan He, Nobuyuki Sakai, Oleg Titov, Fengchun Shu, Hyo-Ryoung Kim, Jungho Cho, Sung-Moon Yoo, Byung-Kyu Choi, Woo Kyoung Lee, Yan Sun, Xiaofeng Mai, Guangli Wang
arxiv-2409-07309.description: Abstract Extending geodetic and astrometric Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) observations from traditional centimeter wavebands to millimeter wavebands offers numerous scientific potentials and benefits. However, it was considered quite challenging due to various factors, including the increased effects of atmospheric opacity and turbulence at millimeter wavelengths.

arxiv-2502-15829.description: Abstract There has been difficulty utilising conditional statements as part of the neural network graph (e.g. if input > x >x , pass input to network N N ). This is due to the inability to backpropagate through branching conditions.

arxiv-2504-05493.title: Neural network-enhanced integrators for simulating ordinary differential equations
arxiv-2504-05493.creator: Amine Othmane, Kathrin Flaßkamp
arxiv-2504-05493.description: Abstract Numerous applications necessitate the computation of numerical solutions to differential equations across a wide range of initial conditions and system parameters, which feeds the demand for efficient yet accurate numerical integration methods. This study proposes a neural network (NN) enhancement of classical numerical integrators.

arxiv-2509-26143.creator: Sasha Bontemps
arxiv-2509-26143.description: Abstract In this article, we study the space of subgroups of non-amenable generalized Baumslag-Solitar groups (GBS groups) of rank d d , that is, groups acting cocompactly on an oriented tree with vertex and edge stabilizers isomorphic to ℤ d \mathbb{Z}^{d} . Our results generalize the study of Baumslag-Solitar groups, and of GBS groups of rank 1 1 .

pmc-11551451.creator: Jaspreet Banga, Taylor Brock-Fisher, Brittany A Petros, Eric Y Dai, Ariana T Leonelli, Sabrina T Dobbins, Katelyn S Messer, Audrey B Nathanson, Amelia Capone, Nancy Littlehale, Viola Appiah-Danquah, Siang Dim, Gage K Moreno, Maura Crowther, Katherine C DeRuff, Bronwyn L MacInnis, Michael Springer, P
pmc-11551451.description: BackgroundHouseholds are a major setting for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infections, but there remains a lack of knowledge regarding the dynamics of viral transmission, particularly in the setting of preexisting SARS-CoV-2 immunity and evolving variants.MethodsWe conducted a prospective, case-ascertained household transmission study in the greater Boston area in March–July 2022.

pmc-11859492.title: Non-compliance as ethical dilemma for kidney transplantation
pmc-11859492.creator: L Rossini Gajsak, L Zibar
pmc-11859492.description: IntroductionAllocating a kidney transplant to a non-compliant recipient could present a triple damage: to the donor (and family of a deceased donor), for the recipient (who will experience rejection) and for another potential recipient on the waiting list (who missed the chance for the transplant).

pmc-12455288.title: Dual-band high-Q quasi-BIC metasurface for refractive index sensing
pmc-12455288.creator: Xunjie Lin, Yunfei Luo, Dongxian Li, Zhe Tang, Yue Li, Kaipeng Liu, Qingguo Du, Changtao Wang, Weisheng Yue
pmc-12455288.description: Sensitive and miniaturized optical sensing device is highly desirable in various biosensing applications. This study reports a dual-band, high-quality-factor (Q factor) quasi-bound states in the continuum (quasi-BIC) metasurface for refractive index sensing, operating across the visible (700–800 nm) and near-infrared (950–1,000 nm) spectral ranges.

pmc-12541945.title: Inflammatory biomarkers in alcohol use disorder: neutrophil/lymphocyte and monocyte/HDL-C ratios as potential diagnostic indicators
pmc-12541945.creator: Omer Acat, Okan Imre
pmc-12541945.description: BackgroundAlcohol use disorder (AUD) constitutes a major global public health concern due to its widespread biological, psychological, and social consequences. Although several biochemical markers—such as gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT), carbohydrate-deficient transferrin (CDT), and mean corpuscular volume (MCV)—have been proposed for AUD diagnosis, their limited specificity can lead to diagnostic inaccuracies.

pmc-12580887.title: Time trends in home dialysis: ERA Registry Figure of the month
pmc-12580887.creator: Vianda S Stel, Alberto Ortiz, Anneke Kramer
pmc-12580887.description: ome haemodialysis (HHD) initiation rate increased between 2012 and 2021, the rate for PD declined, leading to a stable overall home dialysis initiation rate throughout the study period. pmc-12804718.title: Highest early blood pressure within 24 hours and mortality after in-hospital cardiac arrest in the oldest ICU patients: A binational cohort study
pmc-12804718.creator: Je Min Suh, Laurence Weinberg, Jiaying Ye, Stephen Woodford, Anoop N Koshy, Dharshi Karalapillai, Alexandre Joosten, David Pilcher, Dong-Kyu Lee
pmc-12804718.description: Cardiac arrest in nonagenarian and centenarian ICU patients carries high mortality, yet the prognostic role of early blood pressure (BP) parameters remains unclear. While most studies have examined nadir or average values, the clinical significance of the highest very early systolic (SBP), diastolic (DBP), and mean arterial pressure (MAP) has not previously been investigated.

pmc-12995791.title: Targeting magnesium homeostasis: a novel therapeutic strategy for liver diseases
pmc-12995791.creator: Lili Ji, Hanhan Yu, Ruwen Wang, Hongmei Yan, Xiaofeng Yin, Shanshan Guo, Ru Wang
pmc-12995791.description: This review systematically examines a novel therapeutic strategy for liver disease prevention and treatment by targeting magnesium ion homeostasis. Magnesium ions (Mg2+), an essential macromineral, plays a critical role in energy metabolism and enzymatic activity, with its systemic balance maintained through intestinal absorption, renal excretion, and skeletal storage.

pmc-13159228.title: Efficacy of aerobic exercise as a combination therapy for depression compared to standardized therapy: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-13159228.creator: Chengcheng Zhu, Karen M von Deneen, Halijah Binti Ibrahim, Puyan Chi, Mingrui Shao, Weiping Du, Xueying Zhu, Xin Wei, Zeyu Wu, Aiping Chi, Ting Peng, Linfeng Hou
pmc-13159228.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundUtilizing aerobic exercise prevails as a popular choice for physical activity, serving as the predominant exercise intervention for addressing depression. It is also used as supplementary therapy to standardized treatments, including pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, and treatment as usual (TAU). Despite this, the therapeutic mechanism of aerobic exercise as an adjunctive therapy, as well as its interaction with standardized treatments, has not been fully elucidated.
